output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Aria 3 recalibration, drop-off

Last month I told Dana I would write this up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now done eight days of a civil trial, so here it is.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3.

Dropped off: Monday 10/19. Returned: Tuesday 10/27. That is 6 business days against the 10 they quoted.

Work done, per the invoice: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced, internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and internal battery replaced. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

Quoted $285.00. Paid $310.00. The extra $25 was the battery. Gloria found it was holding about 60% of rated capacity and emailed to say she would not go ahead without my approval. I said yes. I appreciated being asked first, and I would rather say so plainly than bury it.

Loaner: yes, a Stenvale Aria 2, issued at drop-off.

Paid personally, as I do for all my equipment. No reimbursement.

The shop: Harbor Point is a two-person operation off York Road in Towson. Parking in back is free. Gloria Ruark did the work.

How it held up: my first full day back was expert testimony, an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke all day, and it has been clean through the rest of the trial. The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made. I have never had that from anyone, and I will keep it with the machine's papers.

What didn't go well:

The loaner's tilt arm would not hold its position. It slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped the writer on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria, and she said they would repair it before it goes out again. It was a nuisance, not a disaster, but check the tilt arm before you leave the shop if you take a loaner.

The phone is the real weakness. The line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that's all. I called on Wednesday 10/21 to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box to leave a message in. Gloria emailed me the next day, so I wasn't left hanging long. Still, if you work a Monday docket, or you need an answer on a Friday, you will not reach them by phone. Email was what actually worked for me.

Dana, to your question: you described a double-stroking number bar on an Aria 3, which is the same machine and close to the same complaint I brought in. They replaced the sensor rather than just adjusting around it, and it has held up under heavy numeric testimony. I would trust them with your Aria. My advice is to drop it off early in the week, ask for the loaner, check the tilt arm before you go, and handle anything time-sensitive by email rather than counting on the phone.

$310 was fair for what was done, and I would go back.

Maureen
